# Example publication profile

A consumer project keeps its publishing limits in a Markdown file like this one and passes
it with `check_publication.py post|article --profile PATH`. Only the first fenced block
tagged `json` is read; everything else in the file is prose for people.

A fenced block of another language comes first and is skipped, even when it shows a
`json` fence of its own:

````text
```json
{"post": {"max_chars": 1}}
```
````

## Machine-readable settings

```json
{
  "post": {"max_chars": 1300, "max_hashtags": 5, "hook_chars": 200},
  "article": {"max_words": 1300, "max_code_blocks": 1, "max_code_lines": 15,
              "min_images": 2, "max_images": 3},
  "forbid_title_terms_from": "unknown keys are ignored (pass the terms with --forbid-title)"
}
```

A later block is ignored, so the settings above stay in force:

```json
{"post": {"max_chars": 1}, "article": {"max_words": 1}}
```
